headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: The last month is clearly weak; the label has not caught up yet

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Keep marketing and acquisition budgets at the planned level, but do not step them up: the last month has been clearly weak, Bitcoin is down about 12% in a week, and the label may turn BEARISH later this week if the weakness lasts. Keep a reserve ready instead of cutting, because the long-run base is still rising; spend it on retention, trust and education now, and on acquisition only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($68,149) and then the 200-day average ($72,802). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: Price is about 18% under its 50-day average, 27 days in a row.
The medium-term reading is in its weak zone; the label waits five days before turning BEARISH.
Fear & Greed is 12 (extreme fear); price is about 5% under its 200-week average.
The long-term base still rises: the 200-day average is up about 6% over 90 days.
watch: The headline still says NEUTRAL, but the last month is clearly weak and price has slipped under its 200-week average ($68,149). Three more weak days would turn the headline BEARISH; a close back above $68,149 and then $72,802 would be the first sign the drop is over.
analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin is in a sharp, fearful pullback, and the safest stance today is to hold steady rather than push. Short term, the mood is very weak: Bitcoin is about $64,741, roughly 18% under its 50-day average after 27 days in a row below it and about 23% under its 30-day high, and the Fear & Greed reading is 12 out of 100 (extreme fear). News is pulling this a little lower too, as PANews reports the Lighter trading venue lost about $15.5M through leaked access keys before returning about $5M and reopening withdrawals. A normal week lately swings about $3,971, so a daily close above $66,750 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week clearly up, a close below $64,150 (the 30-day low) turns it down further, and in between it stays choppy. A calmer few days without new hacks would ease this; until then, campaigns that sell excitement will land badly.

The next month leans down, even though the headline still reads NEUTRAL: the medium-term reading is in its weak zone for a second day, and the label only switches to BEARISH after five days in a row there. Price is about 21% lower than 30 days ago and about 7% lower than 90 days ago, and US spot Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave in the latest day. Bitcoin has to win back $79,007 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed's December 8 meeting is the main scheduled event; keep bigger campaign pushes for after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only just and it is fading: the 200-day average is still rising (about 6% over 90 days), while price is about 11% under it and about 48% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,802 (the 200-day average) again; $68,149 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has now slipped about 5% under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. PANews reports Zelle will issue a dollar stablecoin on Solana and Western Union is using Solana for remittances, a structural plus for crypto, but more weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and be the time to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
